To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a patient presented with superior caval obstruction and was diagnosed with a tumour which was initially thought to be carcinoma of the lung but on immunologic and cytogenic analysis proved to be a B cell lymphoma.

The patient presented with superior venous caval obstruction caused by the tumour which resembled lung carcinoma clinically and histologically, immunological and cytological analysis carried out on the biopsy and the pleural fluid revealed the tumour was Burkitt's lymphoma.
the nature of poorly differentiated tumours can be more clearly identified by immunologic and cytogenic analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new techniques in the study of human tumours.
the development of novel, highly selective and efficient catalysts for the synthesis of fine chemicals, pharmaceuticals and materials.
the identification and characterisation of the molecular and cellular changes that occur in the development of human lymphoma, and the identification of the genetic factors involved in these changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this patient has a B cell lymphoma presenting with superior vena cava syndrome, with the histology and clinical presentation resembling a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, and that the tumour has the translocation t(8; 14) characteristic of Burkitt-like lymphomas.

the mediastinal tumour in this patient is a lymphoma, probably of the Burkitt's lymphoma type, and that it was associated with a t(8; 14) translocation, and that the tumour cells were of B cell origin.
the tumour in this patient is a B cell lymphoma of Burkitt type with a t(8; 14) translocation, and that the tumour is clinically behaving as a poorly differentiated carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunologic and cytogenic studies are very helpful in establishing a definitive diagnosis of the poorly differentiated tumours.
the patient presented with a mediastinal mass, which was initially thought to be a primary lung carcinoma, however, immunologic and molecular cytogenetic analyses revealed it to be a B-cell lymphoma.

we have shown the usefulness of immunological and genetic studies in the diagnosis of a B cell lymphoma masquerading as a carcinoma of the lung and we have shown that the t(8:14) translocation is a common feature of Burkitt-like lymphoma, irrespective of the clinical site of the tumour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nature of many poorly-differentiated tumors may be more clearly determined with the help of cytogenetics and immunological analyses.
immunological and cytogenic analyses should be used more often for the identification of poorly differentiated tumours.
the nature of many poorly defined tumours may be better identified with the aid of immunological and chromosomal analyses.
